name: Republic of the Sudan

areaKm2.note: asOf 2024. Land area 1,868,000 km2 (AG.LND.TOTL.K2, mid); high is surface area incl. inland water 1,878,000 km2 (AG.SRF.TOTL.K2).

population.note: asOf 2025 (World Bank SP.POP.TOTL 51,662,147). Low allows for census uncertainty; high adds one year of growth to 2026 (~2.0%/yr).

activePersonnel.note: IISS Military Balance 2025 p.501 as quoted: SAF 104,300 active (low, pre-war structure) plus 60,000 paramilitary. CIA Factbook 2025: up to 200,000 SAF before 2023. Mid 150,000 and high 300,000 are educated allowances for wartime mobilization and allied forces under SAF command. RSF (up to 100,000 pre-war per CIA; ~100,000+ per Reuters 2023 as quoted on the RSF article) is the enemy and is NOT counted.

trainedReserves.note: Educated guess. Ongoing general mobilization (Popular Resistance) and allied armed movements; no organised trained reserve.

supportPersonnel.note: Mid active 150,000 minus infantry P roles (30,000 + 110,000) = 10,000: air force (~3,000 pre-war), navy, armour/artillery crews, logistics. Wartime manpower is overwhelmingly infantry.

mobilizationRatio.note: Regional analogy: civil-war mobilization of volunteers and militias, constrained by arms supply and the RSF holding Darfur/Kordofan population. Educated judgement.

count.note: Educated guess. SAF infantry with armour/mechanised units (BMP, Mohafiz, Ajban). Pre-war SAF 104,300 (IISS 2025) has expanded through mobilization. (context page: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sudanese_Armed_Forces)

training.note: Rubric 0.25-0.5: three years of urban warfare (Khartoum, Omdurman, Wad Madani, El Obeid).

count.note: Educated guess. SAF light infantry plus allied forces fighting under SAF command: mobilised "Popular Resistance" volunteers, Darfur Joint Forces (SLA-Minnawi, JEM), Islamist brigades (al-Baraa ibn Malik), Beja/eastern militias. Size highly uncertain.

quality.note: Rubric 0.25 minus: small arms and technicals.

training.note: Rubric 0.25-0.5: hastily trained volunteers, forced recruitment reported (CIA Factbook).

count.note: MBT list (pre-war, IISS-derived): T-55 & mods 400 + T-72 230 + Type 96 40 = 670 (high). War losses since April 2023 and RSF captures unknown; mid ~400 is an educated discount. Equipment list details deliveries (T-72M1 130 from Ukraine, Type 85-IIM 50 Al-Bashier).

Equipment list: Caiman ~70 + BMP-1 200+ + BMP-2 100+ + BTR-3 50+ + WZ-523 150+ + Mohafiz-V 100-200+ + NIMR Ajban 70+ + YW531A ~50 = ~840 (BRDM-2 200+ and ~300 M-ATV / 500 Humvee excluded). Mid discounts for war losses.
Equipment list: D-30 300+ + M-46 50 + 2S1 70 + BM-21 120+ + Khalifa SPH (locally produced, few) = ~540+. Mid discounts for war losses and captures.

training.note: Rubric 0.5 minus: in constant use since 2023.

count.note: Inventory (World Air Forces 2026 as quoted): MiG-29SE 10 + MiG-23MS 4 + MiG-21M 4 + F-7M 12 + F-6C 8 = 38 (high). Mid assumes about two thirds serviceable; several lost to RSF MANPADS and drone strikes on bases.
Su-25K 12 + Su-24M 7 + A-5C 20 = 39 (high); An-26/An-12 crude bombers excluded.
Mi-24/35 35 + Mi-8/17/171 24 + Bo-105 20 + IAR-330 16 + Mi-2 6 + Bell 205/212 5 + others 3 = ~109 (World Air Forces 2026 as quoted). Mid for serviceability.
SAF operates Mohajer-6, Wing Loong II, Bayraktar TB2 (deployed in Khartoum, Nov 2024, Sudan Tribune via the article) and Akinci; counts unpublished. Mid is an estimate.
Kurmuk-class (Project 22460) 2 + Swiftships 35 m 2 + Al-Marat 1 + Safeya 2 = 7, plus locally built interceptors.

Equipment list names ZU-23-2 (very many, on technicals), ZPU (4,000+), S-60 (200+) guns; SAM holdings (S-75/S-125 remnants, Pantsir rumoured) unknown. Battery count is an educated guess. (context page: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_equipment_of_the_Sudanese_Armed_Forces)

commandQuality.note: Rubric 0.25-0.5: SAF regained Khartoum (March 2025) and the centre but lost Darfur (El Fasher, Oct 2025); command fragmented across allied militias.

cohesion.note: Rubric 0.25: coalition of army, Islamist brigades and ethnic militias.

morale.note: Rubric 0.5-0.75: existential defence of the state core; recent victories in Khartoum/Gezira.

weapons.note: Anchor 8-9: Soviet/Chinese bulk, Iranian and Turkish UCAVs.

fortification.note: Anchor 8: urban fortification; weak air defence (RSF drone strikes on Port Sudan, May 2025).

gdpPerCapita.note: GDP 77,474,891,940 2011 int$ / population 51,662,147 = 1,500. +/-25% (wartime). Corrected 2026-10-29: values x1.0376 because the rebase factor was an arithmetic error (0.8005); the right factor is 0.8306 (FRED GDPDEF, 2017=100: 2011 91.478 / 2021 110.130). Figures quoted above are before the correction.

gdp.note: asOf 2025 (estimate). World Bank NY.GDP.MKTP.PP.KD 96,783,124,223 x 0.8005 = 77,474,891,940 2011 int$. Wartime collapse (IMF PPP GDP fell from 171 bn 2021 to 120 bn 2025) makes this +/-25%. Corrected 2026-10-29: values x1.0376 because the rebase factor was an arithmetic error (0.8005); the right factor is 0.8306 (FRED GDPDEF, 2017=100: 2011 91.478 / 2021 110.130). Figures quoted above are before the correction.

milSpendShare.note: WARTIME. Last SIPRI/World Bank value 0.93% (2021, low; https://api.worldbank.org/v2/country/SDN/indicator/MS.MIL.XPND.GD.ZS?format=json). No published wartime figure; mid/high are educated guesses for a state at full civil war.

industrialShare.note: asOf 2025: industry incl. construction (and mining/oil where present) 33.6% of GDP (NV.IND.TOTL.ZS). +/-2 points.

foodSurplus.note: Recomputed 2026-10-29 under the definition: 0.0 -> 0.39. Formula: surplus = 1 - a/s, a = farm population share of consumers (proxy: agricultural employment share, World Bank SL.AGR.EMPL.ZS, ILO modelled, https://api.worldbank.org/v2/country/SDN/indicator/SL.AGR.EMPL.ZS), s = domestic production / consumption (calorie self-sufficiency). a = 39.77% (2022). s proxied by cereal self-sufficiency (sorghum, millet, wheat are the staples): 2025 cereal output 5.2 Mt, 22% below 2024, and 2026 import requirement 2.8 Mt (FAO GIEWS, https://www.fao.org/giews/countrybrief/country.jsp?code=SDN&lang=en): s = 5.2/8.0 = 0.65. Mid 1 - 0.398/0.65 = 0.39. Low: a x 1.2, s 0.60 (2026 drought) = 0.2. High: s 0.70 (2024 output 6.67 Mt, same imports) = 0.44. a is 2022, the latest World Bank year. Import dependence: domestic production covers about 65% of domestic calorie supply. Earlier net-trade reading: Educated guess. Famine declared in parts of Darfur/Kordofan (2024-25); Gezira scheme disrupted. Effectively no surplus.

annualCohort.note: asOf 2025. Males reaching military age per year = male population 25,605,038 (SP.POP.TOTL.MA.IN) x share aged 15-19 10.896% / 5 = 557,971. Males only (conscript-pool convention). Range +/-10%.

ifv_apc.note: Educated guess. Military Industry Corporation (Yarmouk, Al-Shajara) produced Khalifa SPH, Sarsar APC and munitions; plants damaged in the war. (context page: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_equipment_of_the_Sudanese_Armed_Forces)

roadKm.note: Road list (2019): 31,000 km total (high), 8,000 km paved (mid). War damage to bridges (Shambat, Jebel Aulia) not reflected.

railKm.note: asOf 2020: 2,747 route-km (World Bank IS.RRS.TOTL.KM). CIA Factbook 7,251 km (2014) spans the range. Mostly 1,067 mm gauge; largely inoperable during the war.

majorPorts.note: CIA Factbook 2024: 4 ports, 2 medium (Port Sudan, Sawakin) plus 2 oil terminals.

merchantTonnage.note: Educated guess. CIA Factbook: 14 ships under the Sudanese flag (2023). (context page: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/factbook/factbook.json/master/africa/su.json)

supplyRangeKm.note: Educated guess. Truck and technical columns; long desert lines to Darfur.

draftAnimals.note: Educated guess. Very large camel and donkey herds; animals are used for transport by both sides. Not from FAO data.

nuclearWarheads.note: Non-nuclear-weapon state (NPT); not listed by FAS Status of World Nuclear Forces.

homeDefense.note: Rubric 1.1: familiar terrain and local supply; civil war means the "home" advantage is contested.

notes: WARTIME snapshot (civil war since 15 April 2023), asOf 2025 World Bank data with a 2026 order of battle. This snapshot represents the internationally recognised state and the Sudanese Armed Forces (SAF, led by Gen. al-Burhan) with the forces fighting under it. The Rapid Support Forces (RSF, Gen. Hemedti), a paramilitary created in 2013 that turned on the SAF, hold most of Darfur (El Fasher fell Oct 2025) and parts of Kordofan and declared a rival "Government of Peace and Unity" (2025); RSF manpower (100,000+ pre-war) and equipment are excluded and would need their own snapshot. The SAF retook Khartoum in March 2025. Population convention: whole internationally recognised territory (World Bank), although roughly a third is RSF-held; displacement exceeds 10 million. All equipment counts are pre-war IISS-derived or delivery-based figures discounted for unknown losses (grade C/D). Money in 2011 int$ via derived:ppp-rebase-2011 (+/-25%). milSpendShare low = last peacetime figure, mid = wartime educated guess. Doctrine archetype-insurgent because irregular and militia forces dominate both sides of the fighting. UN arms embargo on Darfur since 2005.
